name: Brain Arteriovenous Malformation

criteria.description: Identification of a nidus of abnormal arteriovenous shunting on cerebral angiography or MRI/MRA
Presence of neurological symptoms such as hemorrhage, seizures, or focal neurological deficits attributable to AVM
Exclusion of other vascular malformations or tumors by imaging and clinical evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of AVM nidus plus compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on neuroimaging; histopathology is rarely required.

imaging: Cerebral angiography showing nidus of tangled vessels with early venous drainage
MRI/MRA demonstrating abnormal vascular structures and flow voids
CT scan showing intracranial hemorrhage or calcifications
genetic: Mostly sporadic; rare familial cases reported with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT)
other: Audible cranial bruit on auscultation over lesion site

distinguishingFeatures: Saccular aneurysm without nidus of abnormal vessels
No early venous drainage on angiography
Typically presents with subarachnoid hemorrhage rather than intraparenchymal hemorrhage
No large feeding arteries or early venous drainage
MRI shows 'popcorn-like' lesion with hemosiderin rim
Less likely to cause high-flow shunting symptoms

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache with neurological deficit
New onset focal seizures in young adult
Signs of intracranial hemorrhage on imaging
references: Al-Shahi Salman R et al. Diagnosis and management of brain arteriovenous malformations: a scientific statement for healthcare professionals from the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association. Stroke. 2017.
Meyers PM et al. Brain arteriovenous malformations. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2021.
